text: right... im saying how it loads in the game data not how it skips the v8 runtime
resolution: Cloned world_loader.zig's DATA-LOAD path into TypeScript and wired it behind /test. New cart/hmsc-int/editors/play/tsLoader/: decode.ts is the byte-exact twin of constructor.zig (decodes the RJMP map container's INSTANCES/MATERIALS/MATERIAL_REFS/COLLIDERS/PHYSICS_CONFIG/HEIGHTFIELDS/FLORA/ENVIRONMENT lumps into a flat LoadedScene); buildBuckets.ts groups decoded rows into Scene3D.Instances batches (the loader's buildShapeBatches); WorldLoaderView.tsx runs the full bake->decode->batch path in V8 and draws it with the host-side native FreeFly camera (no per-frame React) plus a load-cost HUD; PlayTestRoute wraps /test with an F3 toggle to A/B PlayRoute vs the TS loader. Verified: decode round-trip test 6/6, cart bundles clean, headless load bench = ~138ms/M instances (500k in 69ms). Remaining for the user: run rjit dev hmsc-int, /test, press F3, compare frame rate vs /compiled — that interactive A/B is the actual answer to whether it performs as well as native.
